name: Autograph
known: Wikipedia says the board renamed it Autograph ABP in 2002, and that Mark Sealy became director in 1991.

name: British Museum
known: Founded by Act of Parliament on 7 June 1753 on the collection of Sir Hans Sloane.
Chair George Osborne, director Nicholas Cullinan (Wikipedia; 2025/26 accounts).

name: Camden Art Centre
known: Martin Clark has been director since 2017, after Jenni Lomax (1990 to 2017).

The thank-you page lists a 60th Anniversary Building Acquisition Fund with these founders: Antony Gormley and Vicken Parsons, Alexandra and Guy Halamish and Donald Porteous; building benefactors A4 Arts Foundation, Erin Bell and Michael Cohen, Batia and Idan Ofer, The Foyle Foundation and Texel Foun

name: Chisenhale Gallery
known: Edward Gillman became director in March 2025, after Zoé Whitley stepped down in February 2025.
May Calil chairs the trustees (2025 accounts, Charity Commission data).

name: Delfina Foundation
known: Named for its founder, who died in 2022 aged 94.
Aaron Cezar is the founding director.
The founder gave seed money and rent-free space from 2007; that support ended in 2020, and the foundation now raises all its income (stated by the space).
Building: the founder owned it and it passed to her grandchildren (The Art Newspaper, 2024).

name: Design Museum
known: Founded in 1989 by Sir Terence Conran, with Stephen Bayley as first chief executive, in a former banana warehouse at Shad Thames.
Tim Marlow has been director since 2019.

The museum lost £2,026,462 in the year to March 2019 and the Conran Foundation lent it £3 million; the annual report, written by the then chair Lord Mandelson, called its finances "not sustainable in the medium term" (Dezeen, 2019).
Stuart Roden has chaired the board since July 2023 (trustees page).
Has a three-year strategic partnership, from March 2025, with Shenzhen Bay Culture Square (D-Bay); its founder Terence Conran is a person.

name: Dulwich Picture Gallery
known: John Soane designed the top-lit building and a mausoleum where the founders are buried.
Jennifer Scott has been director since April 2017.
Dame Janet Vitmayer chairs the trustees.
Deputy director Chantelle Culshaw chairs the Christina Smith Foundation, which gave £75,000 to the Future Plan (related-party note).

name: English National Ballet
known: Watkin has been artistic director since 2023, after Tamara Rojo (2012 to 2022).
It is named for the family of Sean Mulryan, chairman of the developer Ballymore (thank-you page).

name: Gasworks
known: Director: Robert Leckie succeeded Alessio Antoniolli in 2024; nine trustees are listed on OpenCharities, from Charity Commission data, including Alexa Waley-Cohen (appointed March 2025).

name: Goldsmiths CCA
known: Sarah McCrory is director (stated by the space).

name: Mosaic Rooms
known: Trustees are Dr Selma Taysir Dabbagh (chair), Lamiaa Soliman (treasurer), Celeste Ricci, Maisha Akil Scafe-Smith, Dr Samaneh Moafi, Christopher Rawcliffe, Marwan Kaabour and Zainab Sahar Beyad (Mosaic Rooms website).
Director Pip Day was previously director of the Leonard & Bina Ellen Art Gallery at Concordia University in Montreal, which dismissed her in late 2024 after less than six months.

The Mosaic Rooms re-incorporated as a charity so that it can seek private philanthropy and public grants; director Pip Day says the goal was to transition into a public institution that belongs to London rather than to the family (The Art Newspaper).

The Qattan family money: Wikipedia's article on Omar al-Qattan says his father Abdel Mohsin Al-Qattan first joined the Kuwaiti government as a senior manager and later founded a construction company, and that Omar has been deputy chair of the family firm, Al-Hani Construction and Trading, since 2005
Director Pip Day's 2024 dismissal from a Concordia gallery concerned a film screening, not funding.
